items.prompt: Each input fits within plus/minus 1000000, but n can reach 200000. Why not use signed 64-bit for every exact predicate product?

options.text: Because Python int also overflows at 2^63.
options.why: Python integer arithmetic is not limited to signed 64-bit; this claim confuses the two representations.

options.text: Because a single input already exceeds signed 64-bit.
options.why: Each input is small. The danger is in accumulated products and squared numerators.

options.text: Because n*Q and squared deviations can exceed 9.22e18.
options.why: Full-bound exact products can be around 1e23. A fixed-width port needs sufficiently promoted wider arithmetic.

options.text: Because replacing all products by float proves exact equality.
options.why: Floating conversion loses the exact strict-boundary guarantee that the companion arithmetic is designed to provide.

items.explanation: Full-bound exact products can be around 1e23. A fixed-width port needs sufficiently promoted wider arithmetic.
